newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas softens before close on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas softens before close on profit-taking.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures drifted lower late Friday, as traders took profits ahead of the weekend after this week's weather-driven rally, industry sources said.
At 1440 EST, February was down 12.1 cents to $3.36 per million British thermal units, while March was 15.6 cents lower at $2.93. Most others were down slightly.
"The speculative interest in the market is really causing a little havoc. They're not in it for the long-term, one futures trader said, noting late profit-taking was pressuring the market late.
"It's not a highly liquid market though," he said.
As of 1410 EST, NYMEX said 32,273 Hub contracts had traded.
Forecasts calling for below-normal temperatures throughout most of the U.S. next week should keep both the futures and cash markets fairly strong, most traders agreed.

Technically, traders still pegged February support in the remaining gap between $3.11 and $3.25, with better buying likely in the $2.60s. Resistance was seen in the $3.80-3.84 area and at $3.96. The contract high is $4.02.

In the cash, most Gulf prices were up about 30 cents to the $3.85-3.90 range. Midcontinent prices gained about a $1 to the high-$4 area. At the Chicago city-gate, cash prices ranged from a high of $6.50 to a low of $4.50, while New York city-gate values were talked around $4.50.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas were untraded at 1450 EST.
On the KCBT, February retreated to $3.18, down 14 cents, while March fell 28 cents to $2.65. The East/West spread widened by 1.9 cents to 18.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
Physical prices at Waha for the weekend gained about 45 cents Friday to the $4.10-4.15 range.
